transcript:
Meeting header: Tue Sep 16 2025 15:00 PDT | Duration 48m | Recording: Zoom | Notes: quick intro call, AE+SE + infra leads
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nandakumar (IronVeil Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (IronVeil CTO), Ravi Patel (IronVeil Infra Lead)
Shared artifacts referenced: 1) Redwood_onramp_deck_v3 (link sent in chat), 2) sample_benchmarks.csv (gdrive link), 3) SOC2-summary.pdf (will be shared)

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, our AE for platform partnerships, with Diego our solutions engineer.
00:12 Priya Nandakumar: hi thanks, appreciate it. We're excited to see how you might fit into our marketplace flows, so quick context — IronVeil runs a multi-tenant SaaS marketplace, we onboard third-party models and also run some internal models.
00:22 Maya Chen: awesome, quick high-level question — are you primarily looking for a managed API (hosted) or are you evaluating dedicated / private for data isolation?
00:30 Liam O'Connor: right now it's leaning dedicated or private, because some of our partners have strict residency and they want keys in our KMS. But cost is a factor so we're open to a Hosted with VPC peering if that hits the numbers.
00:44 Diego Alvarez: ok, helpful — when you say KMS, is that cloud provider KMS (like AWS KMS) or an HSM you manage?
00:52 Ravi Patel: it's a mix — most are AWS KMS, but we do have one partner wanting HSM-backed keys and a localized deployment for EU data.
01:01 Maya Chen: got it — so we should walk through our Private deployment + VPC options and the Dedicated reserved capacity as two distinct patterns. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and predictable unit cost; Private gives you that HSM/KMS control. Hosted can be configured with VPC egress and endpoint peering but there's tradeoffs.
01:20 Liam O'Connor: can you ballpark the latency delta between Hosted and Dedicated? Our SLAs are tight for inference under 200ms P50 for small responses.
01:29 Diego Alvarez: sure, roughly speaking Hosted on our best regions usually gets you 60–120ms p50 for small generative prompts, Dedicated (co-located GPUs) can shave that to 30–80ms depending on GPU and batch sizing; but if you enable heavy batching you'll push p95 up. Also sequence length matters, and our kernel selection adapts.
01:51 Priya Nandakumar: when you say kernel selection, are you referring to optimizations for quantized models? We have a mix of FP16 and some int8-ish quantized variants.
02:01 Diego Alvarez: yeah, we do quantization-friendly execution paths, and the runtime will pick kernels based on model arch and seq length. There's some heuristics; we can show profiling.
02:11 Priya Nandakumar: good, because cost for us is super important — these marketplace calls are often bursty. Any recommendations around autoscale / burst pools?
02:21 Maya Chen: we offer configurable autoscaling and a burst capacity option for Dedicated. For bursty workloads we recommend a small reserved pool + burst policy to on-demand capacity. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/caching profiles based on sample traces to reduce unit cost.
02:38 Liam O'Connor: how do you handle prefix caching and KV? We can't afford full token cost for repeated system prompts.
02:46 Diego Alvarez: automatic prefix / KV caching is supported. It reduces the token cost and latency for repeated contexts; there are config knobs for reuse windows. Sometimes the transcriptions call it "KV cash" in older docs — you'll see typos.
02:58 Priya Nandakumar: ha, committed typo noted. Another item — security and audit logs. Our compliance requires per-tenant audit logs for inference requests and redaction controls.
03:09 Maya Chen: we surface per-token traces and request-level audit logs in Redwood Console; we also support log retention policies and can integrate with your SIEM. For Private we can ship audit logs to your S3 or to a SIEM over a secure endpoint.
03:25 Ravi Patel: ok, do you have SOC 2 attestation and penetration test reports we can share with partners?
03:30 Maya Chen: yes, will share SOC 2 summary and the redacted pentest report. I'll add that to the drive link.
03:37 Liam O'Connor: switching to infra — our infra team currently uses a mix of A100 and older V100s; long-term we may standardize on L40s. Any model compatibility problems there?
03:47 Diego Alvarez: Redwood's runtime supports a broad set — A100 and L40 are great. Older V100s are fine for some models but you might see perf regression. Also quantization can change kernel paths; we'll validate in a quick perf run.
04:01 Priya Nandakumar: what's your usual POC length and acceptance criteria? We want to limit to a 2-week technical POC ideally, with success criteria around: 1) throughput meets x rps at 200ms p50, 2) cost per inference within target, 3) integration with our KMS and audit log export.
04:16 Maya Chen: that's reasonable. Typical POCs are 1–3 weeks. We do an initial baseline benchmark on our end and then a joint validation with your traces. Acceptance criteria you listed are the right sort. We'll propose a 2-week POC scope.
04:28 Ravi Patel: curious about routing and fallback — if dedicated capacity is saturated, can traffic failover to hosted? We need graceful degradation.
04:36 Diego Alvarez: yes, smart routing supports fallback policies to compatible model variants in Hosted or another region. You can set cost vs latency routing priorities.
04:45 Priya Nandakumar: are there any hard limits for multi-tenancy and per-tenant isolation? We can't have KV cache bleed between tenants.
04:52 Maya Chen: isolation is per-customer and per-model. For multi-tenant you can use per-tenant cache namespaces and RBAC, and for Private you'd get stronger network and tenancy controls.
05:05 Liam O'Connor: ok, budget — what are the rough numbers for dedicated reserved pool vs hosted per-token for our estimated 500k tokens/day?
05:12 Maya Chen: rough sketch — Hosted per-token pricing can vary but say $0.0003–$0.0006 per input token depending on model; Dedicated amortizes infra so at your scale it may be 20–40% cheaper but with a monthly commit. I'll send a model-specific cost sheet.
05:27 Priya Nandakumar: who else from Redwood will be involved if we proceed? We want a single technical point of contact.
05:33 Maya Chen: Diego will be your SE lead during POC and I'll coordinate commercial + onboarding. Post-POC we'll loop in Customer Success for runbook and SRE contacts.
05:43 Ravi Patel: little nit: we need to validate network egress, NAT, and private endpoints. Can you provide a network diagram for VPC peering?
05:51 Diego Alvarez: yes, we'll share a VPC peering + SAML diagram. Also note some older docs call it "VPC peering shims" — ignore the phrasing, it's the same concept.
06:03 Priya Nandakumar: timeline — we're trying to pilot with one partner in October. Is that feasible?
06:09 Maya Chen: if we get your workload traces this week and agree on a POC scope we'll aim to start the POC in early October.
06:17 Liam O'Connor: ok great. quick question on model variants — can Redwood host third-party models from container images or only from model repos?
06:25 Diego Alvarez: we support model artifacts from repo formats and can also pull containerized runtimes for certain private deployments. We'll need to validate image size and GPU bindings.
06:34 Priya Nandakumar: perfect. that's most of our list. Anything else?
06:38 Maya Chen: last thing — any concerns about vendor lock-in? We support export of traces, cached keys references (not raw secrets), and you can pin to model versions for rollbacks.
06:50 Ravi Patel: that's reassuring. thanks.
06:54 Maya Chen: ok quick recap and next steps: I'll send pricing and SOC2 + VPC docs by Friday (2025-09-19), Diego will prepare the infra checklist and benchmark questions, Priya will share traces and current GPU inventory. We'll schedule the infra deep-dive for week of 2025-09-22.
07:10 Priya Nandakumar: thanks everyone, that works.
07:13 Liam O'Connor: thanks Maya, Diego.
07:15 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had some label swaps (Speaker 2 vs names) and occasional mis-heard terms ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache").
